scope: Current bounded prototypes and the three consumer profiles; research dispositions authorize no production adoption. Final correctness/compatibility checks remain prerequisites.

records.rationale: The checked-view pattern is coherent under the listed correspondence assumptions, but this implementation still performs full J and snapshot checks and retains Core evidence construction. Its measured total cost is higher than the forced reference in the baseline cases; these results do not evaluate an efficient unchecked IVM implementation.

A requires an established meaning/anchor and controlled maintenance. Its retained views are not independent proof authority for an untrusted producer. A fresh consumer must reconstruct or independently check those premises.
Maintained views alone supply no succinct accepted history certificate. Complete audit output and the implemented initialization/history checks remain material work.
This full-snapshot producer plus independent Core recomputation is additional execution/checking work, not a demonstrated local performance improvement.

The whole-history checker is a useful exact independent baseline and rejects altered claims without trusting A or producer approval. Cheaper sparse checking still needs authenticated access, complete coverage and an exact identity/error correspondence argument. No such protocol is implemented here.

The current checker reconstructs and recomputes the full claimed history. Replacing repeated per-witness replay with one fresh Store removes incidental duplication but does not make full-history verification succinct.

Real proof construction is feasible for the bounded circuit, but it neither removes Core execution/evidence work nor demonstrates a useful local transition cost. Native and proof capacity workloads must not be treated as an identical performance baseline.

Fresh consumers actually verify bounded Nova proofs and exact expected Core bridges. This establishes feasibility under explicit implementation/crypto assumptions; the current consumer still redoes Core work and has substantial parameter costs. It is not a replacement for Safety Model certification or a demonstrated production verifier.

Recursive verification at fixed circuit capacity is distinct from the complete Core claim. The full Core identity bridge remains necessary and history dependent. A future protocol must prove that bridge or explicitly version the evidence/identity contract, with separate availability and authorization obligations. No hybrid is adopted.
